findings.title: Adding `order()` as an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `CryptoProvider` is a ServiceLoader SPI, so providers compiled against the previous interface do not implement this new abstract method. Such providers now fail to compile when rebuilt and can throw `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` compares them with another provider (for example, the newly added authz-client provider). Make this a default method with a backward-compatible priority (such as 0), so existing provider implementations remain usable.

findings.title: Equal provider priorities make FIPS selection depend on classpath order
findings.body: The built-in Default, Elytron, and FIPS providers all return priority 200. For providers with the same priority, this sort preserves the ServiceLoader encounter order, which is determined by classpath/resource order rather than an explicit security policy. Consequently, when both the default and FIPS service descriptors are visible, the default provider can be selected and the FIPS provider merely logged as ignored; previously this unsafe combination failed fast. Give the intended FIPS provider a distinct higher priority or reject ties for the highest priority.

findings.title: The selected authz crypto provider cannot perform documented JWT client authentication
findings.body: `AuthzClient.create` initializes this provider in a standalone authz-client runtime, but this implementation throws `UnsupportedOperationException` for both PEM handling here and JWS signature creation in `getSignature` (line 219). The authz client documents JWT client credentials as a supported credential type; that flow must parse the configured private key and sign a client assertion, so it will fail once this provider is selected. Provide the standard JCA/PEM implementations for these operations, or avoid installing this incomplete provider as the global CryptoIntegration provider.

findings.title: ES384 and ES512 tests do not use their required elliptic curves
findings.body: All three tests use an uninitialized generic EC key generator, which normally produces a P-256 key. Thus the ES384 and ES512 cases sign with P-256 coordinates padded to the requested output length, rather than exercising P-384 and P-521 coordinate sizes and DER edge cases. The test also only checks conversion round-tripping, not whether the reconstructed signature verifies. Initialize keys explicitly to secp256r1, secp384r1, and secp521r1 respectively and verify the converted signature.
